caption: 01 · RETRIEVE — Can the right record be found?. Identifiers, dates, makers, materials, controlled vocabulary, file relationships, and search pathways determine whether memory is available at the moment of decision.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping can the right record be found? within Archive as Design Employee.

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · READ — Can someone understand why it matters?. A sketch, fitting note, failed sample, or garment becomes more useful when the record preserves the question it answered—not only what it looks like.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping can someone understand why it matters? within Archive as Design Employee.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · TRANSFORM — Can the archive generate difference?. The strongest use is not literal revival. It is recovery of a method, constraint, construction problem, or unresolved question that can be recomposed for a new context.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping can the archive generate difference? within Archive as Design Employee.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · CITE — Can the new work show its lineage?. Source identifiers, rights decisions, credits, and transformation notes let inspiration remain accountable. Citation does not weaken originality; it distinguishes research from extraction.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
